Atom Economy Maximize the incorporation of reactants into the final product. Aim for 100% atom economy using addition/rearrangement reactions. 3. Safer Synthesis Minimize or avoid hazardous substances in synthesis. Example: Use CO, instead of toxic phosgene in polyurethane synthesis. 4. Safe Products Products should be effective but with reduced toxicity. Minimize harmful side effects on users and the environment. 5. Design Benign Chemicals Use safer solvents/reaction conditions. Design for Energy Efficiency Reduce energy intensity by using catalysts (e.g., bio-catalysts) and modern methods like microwave or ultrasound irradiation. 7. Use of Renewable Feedstock Prefer renewable raw materials like biomass over non-renewable sources such as coal and petroleum. 8. Reduce Derivatives Avoid unnecessary derivatization steps (e.g., blocking/protecting groups) to minimize waste and enhance atom efficiency. 9. Catalysis Use catalysts to accelerate reactions, reduce energy use, and achieve high yields with recyclable, selective reactions. 10. Design for Degradation Products should degrade into harmless substances after use to prevent environmental accumulation (e.g., pesticides, polymers). 11. Pollution Prevention Employ real-time monitoring and control of processes to prevent hazardous substances. Recycle unreacted chemicals. 12. Accident Prevention Choose chemicals and processes to minimize risks of accidents like fires, explosions, and toxic releases. Equip facilities with safety measures.
